topic: Systems of two linear equations --- the intersection is the solution
subtitle: The point that makes both equations true at once

problems.desc: Part (b): explanation of what the crossing point of lines A and B means for the two equations. Full credit requires the student to say that the point lies on both lines at once, so its coordinates make both equations true, and that is what it means to be the solution of the system. Accept an answer that substitutes the coordinates into both equations as the explanation. Do not accept 'it is where they cross' with no link to the equations.

problems.slot: (b) what it means about the gyms
problems.desc: Part (b): explanation of what a system with no solution means for the two gyms. Full credit requires the student to say that both gyms charge the same amount per class, so the cheaper one stays exactly 15 dollars cheaper no matter how many classes are taken, and the two cost lines never meet. Accept a graphical answer that says the lines are parallel because the rates are equal and the starting fees differ. Do not accept 'no solution' with no reference to the gyms.

Part (b): explanation of why the pair the student claimed is not the solution. Full credit requires the student to substitute it into both equations and report that it satisfies the first but not the second, and to say that a solution of a system must satisfy every equation, not just one. Accept an answer that identifies which equation fails and by how much. Do not accept 'it is wrong' with no substitution shown.

Part (b): explanation of how the Graph Bank shows the answer to part (a). Full credit requires the student to say that lines A and D climb at the same rate, so they stay the same distance apart and never cross, and that a system whose graphs never cross has no solution. Accept an answer that reads the constant vertical gap of 3 units off the grid. Do not accept 'they are parallel' with no statement of what that means for the system.

problems.slot: (b) what it means for a swimmer
problems.desc: Part (b): explanation of what the intersection means for someone choosing a pool plan. Full credit requires the student to say that at the intersection the two plans cost the same, and to name which plan is cheaper on each side of it: pay-per-visit is cheaper below that number of visits and the membership is cheaper above it. Accept a graphical answer describing which line is lower on each side. Do not accept only the coordinates repeated in words.
